faq: What is Nmap?

Nmap (Network Mapper) is the standard open-source tool for discovering hosts and services on a network. It sends packets, reads the replies, and reports which hosts are up, which ports are open, and which software is behind them. Every security team maps its own network with it before attackers do.
Is Nmap illegal?

No. Nmap is a legitimate open-source scanner. Running it against networks you do not own or lack permission to test can be treated as unauthorized probing, so stick to your own lab and the official practice target scanme.nmap.org.
What is the difference between -sn, -sS and -sV?
-sn is ping-scan: only find live hosts, no port scan. -sS is the SYN stealth scan of the top 1,000 ports. -sV adds version detection, asking open ports which software and version they run.
What is a SYN scan?

A SYN scan starts the TCP handshake but never completes it: SYN goes out, SYN-ACK comes back, Nmap sends RST instead of ACK. The port state is learned without a full connection, so it is fast and quieter than a connect scan.
How do I scan safely without knocking things over?

Scan your own lab or scanme.nmap.org, use default timing (-T3), and avoid -T5 aggressive timing plus --min-rate floods against anything fragile. Printers, cameras and old industrial gear can crash under fast scans.
What is OS detection (-O)?

OS detection compares subtle TCP/IP behaviors — initial TTL, window size, option order — against a fingerprint database and guesses the operating system, like Linux 5.x or Windows 10. It needs at least one open and one closed port to work well.
How do I find live hosts on my WiFi?
Run nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24 on your own network. Nmap ARPs every address and lists the ones that answer with their MAC vendor. That is how you spot an unknown device on your home WiFi.
How do I defend against Nmap scans?
Close ports you do not need, firewall the rest, run fail2ban to block repeat probers, and monitor logs. You cannot stop someone scanning you, but you can give them nothing interesting to find.

install_note: On Kali Linux Nmap is pre-installed — nmap --version is enough to confirm. On Debian/Ubuntu and Termux install the nmap package.
issues: Permission denied on SYN scan
SYN scans need raw sockets: re-run with sudo, or use -sT connect scan which works unprivileged but is louder.
All ports show filtered
A firewall is dropping your probes (or you scanned the wrong address). From your own lab, check the target firewall rules and your VPN routing.
-O needs root and guesses wrong
OS detection needs one open and one closed port plus root. Give it both, and treat the result as a best guess, not gospel.
Scan takes forever on some hosts
Down hosts are re-probed by default. Add --max-retries 1 -T4 for lab sweeps, and always use -sn first so you only port-scan live hosts.

steps.box: -sn sends no port probes — it only asks who is alive. Use it first so you never waste a port scan on dead addresses.
steps.code:
nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24
# 5 hosts up: router, laptop, phone...

steps.sub: Who is alive on the network

steps.box: open answered, closed refused, filtered means a firewall dropped the probe. The official practice target scanme.nmap.org exists exactly for this.
steps.code:

# 22/tcp open  ssh
# 80/tcp open  http

steps.box: The version string is gold: it tells you exactly which CVEs to check. That is why admins patch — and why they hide banners where they can.
steps.code:
nmap -sV -O scanme.nmap.org
# 80/tcp open  Apache httpd 2.4.49
# OS: Linux 5.x
steps.desc: Ask open ports what software they run, and guess the OS:
steps.title: Step 3 — Detect Versions + OS

steps.box: NSE turns Nmap into a vulnerability checker: http-title grabs page titles, vuln scripts cross-check versions against known CVEs. Always stay on targets you own.
steps.code:
nmap --script vuln scanme.nmap.org
# CVE-2021-41773: Apache path traversal FOUND

desc: Step-by-step SQLMap reference: find, confirm and exploit SQL injection on lab targets (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop). Educational use only.
disclaimer: This documentation is provided strictly for educational and authorized purposes. SQLMap automates database theft, so use it only on your own lab apps (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop) or targets with written permission. Testing anyone else is illegal. The author and this site are not responsible for any misuse.
faq: What is SQLMap?

SQLMap is an open-source tool that automates SQL injection: you give it a URL with a parameter, it confirms the injection, fingerprints the database, and can list tables and dump data. What takes hours by hand takes it minutes.
Is SQLMap illegal?

The tool is legal and used in authorized audits. Pointing it at any site you do not own or lack permission to test is illegal — injection dumps real user data. Practice on DVWA or OWASP Juice Shop running on your own machine.
What does --dbs do?
--dbs lists all databases on the server after SQLMap confirms injection. Then -D picks one database, --tables lists its tables, -T picks a table, and --dump pulls the rows.
What is the difference between --batch and interactive mode?
By default SQLMap asks questions mid-run (which payload? try harder?). --batch answers yes to everything so a lab run finishes unattended. Add --random-agent to rotate the user-agent string.
What is tamper scripts (--tamper)?
Tamper scripts rewrite payloads to slip past weak filters — for example space2comment swaps spaces for comments. They beat naive keyword blocklists in labs, not real WAFs.
How do I point SQLMap at a login form?
Capture the POST request (browser devtools or Burp), save it to a file, and run sqlmap -r request.txt -p username. The -p flag tells SQLMap which parameter to inject so it ignores the rest.
What is --risk and --level?
--level 1-5 controls how many parameters and headers get tested; --risk 1-3 controls how dangerous the payloads are (risk 3 can UPDATE/DELETE data). Keep both at 1 in shared labs.
How do I protect my own app from SQLMap?

Use prepared statements (parameterized queries) everywhere, give the app DB user minimum privileges, put a WAF like ModSecurity in front, and log UNION/SELECT probe patterns. SQLMap then finds nothing to exploit.

Point it at a DVWA URL and confirm the injection.
Dump a lab table and try tamper scripts.
Fix your own apps with prepared statements + WAF.
install_cmd:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install sqlmap
install_note: On Kali Linux SQLMap is pre-installed — sqlmap --version confirms it. Debian/Ubuntu users install the sqlmap package, or clone GitHub for the latest.
issues: No parameter found / not injectable
SQLMap needs a * marked parameter or a -p name. Save the full POST request with -r, mark the field, and point -p at it.
Target times out or blocks you
DVWA security must be LOW for basic demos, and some setups rate-limit. Lower --threads to 1, add --delay 1, and check the lab app is actually running.
--dump returns empty tables
You picked the wrong database with -D. Run --dbs first, then -D <name> --tables, then -T <table> --dump — one level at a time.
Tamper script breaks the payload
Some tampers conflict with each other or the target stack. Use one tamper at a time (space2comment first) and drop --tamper entirely to confirm the base injection works.

overview_p2: Injection is still a top web risk because one concatenated query exposes the whole database. Learn the attack on DVWA so you can kill the bug class with prepared statements in your own code.

steps.box: SQLMap fingerprints the backend (MySQL, Postgres...) and injection type (boolean, UNION, time-based). Confirm this step on DVWA with security set to LOW.
steps.code:
sqlmap -u "http://localhost/dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1&Submit=Submit" --batch
# GET parameter id is MySQL >= 5 injectable
steps.desc: Confirm the injection on your DVWA lab:
steps.title: Step 1 — Confirm Injection

steps.box: Walk the hierarchy: server to databases to tables to columns. Each flag narrows one level — never jump straight to --dump or you will miss the layout.
steps.code:
sqlmap -u "...id=1&Submit=Submit" --dbs --batch
# available databases: dvwa, information_schema
sqlmap -u "..." -D dvwa --tables --batch
# users, guestbook
steps.desc: List databases, then tables inside dvwa:
steps.title: Step 2 — Enumerate

steps.box: Watch how hashes come back — MD5 unsalted in DVWA falls instantly to a wordlist. That is the lesson: hash right (bcrypt) and limit what the app user can read.
steps.code:
sqlmap -u "..." -D dvwa -T users --dump --batch
# 5 rows: admin, gordonb, ... password hashes
steps.desc: Dump the lab users table (your own DVWA only):
steps.title: Step 3 — Dump Lab Data

steps.box: Tampers beat classroom filters, not production WAFs. If the base injection fails without --tamper, fix the request (cookies, login, -p) before blaming the filter.
steps.desc: Try a tamper script against a filtered lab input:
steps.title: Step 4 — Tamper Scripts

desc: Step-by-step Hydra reference: brute-force SSH, FTP and web logins on your own lab VMs with wordlists. Educational use only.
disclaimer: This documentation is provided strictly for educational and authorized purposes. Hydra guesses passwords at scale, so use it only on your own lab VMs (Metasploitable, DVWA) or targets with written permission. Attacking real logins is illegal. The author and this site are not responsible for any misuse.
faq: What is Hydra?

Hydra (THC-Hydra) is the classic online password guesser: it tries username/password pairs against live login services — SSH, FTP, HTTP forms, RDP and dozens more. You give it a target, a user list and a password list; it reports what worked.
Is Hydra illegal?

The tool is legal for audits. Using it against logins you do not own or lack permission to test is illegal — even one guess at someone else's account counts. Practice on Metasploitable or your own VMs.
What do -l, -L, -p, -P mean?
-l is one fixed username, -L is a file of usernames. -p is one fixed password, -P is a file of passwords (like rockyou.txt). So -l admin -P rockyou.txt tries admin against every line of the list.
What does -t do?
-t sets parallel tasks (default 16). More tasks = faster but noisier and more likely to lock accounts or get blocked. In labs 4-16 is typical; against anything shared keep it low.
How do I attack a web login form?

Use the http-post-form module with the path, the POST body using ^USER^ and ^PASS^ placeholders, and the failure string: hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt target http-post-form "/login:user=^USER^&pass=^PASS^:Login failed".
Why did Hydra find nothing?
Either the credentials are not in your lists, the failure string is wrong (for web forms), or the service rate-limits/blocks you. Verify the login manually first, then check -V verbose output.
What is the difference between Hydra and Hashcat?
Hydra guesses against a LIVE service over the network (online, slow, lockout risk). Hashcat cracks stolen hash files offline on GPU (fast, no lockouts). Different phases, often used together.
How do I protect my logins from Hydra?
Long unique passwords from a manager, 2FA on everything, fail2ban or rate-limiting after a few failures, and key-only SSH with PasswordAuthentication off. Any one of these breaks naive brute force.

install_cmd:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install hydra
install_note: On Kali Linux Hydra is pre-installed — hydra -h confirms it. Debian/Ubuntu users install the hydra package (rockyou.txt ships with Kali wordlists).
issues: Hydra finds nothing on SSH
The password is not in your list, or fail2ban jailed you mid-run. Check verbose (-V) output, try the known lab password manually, and unban your IP on the lab VM.
Web form always says success
Your failure string is wrong — Hydra keys off it. View page source after a bad login, copy the exact error text, and put it after the last colon.
Connection errors / timeouts
Wrong port or service name, or -t too high for the lab VM. Start with -t 1 -V -s <port> and confirm with a manual login first.
rockyou.txt not found
On Kali extract it: gunzip /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt.gz. Elsewhere download SecLists and pass the full path to -P.

steps.box: -V shows each attempt, -f stops at the first hit, -t 4 keeps the lab VM happy. Metasploitable's msfadmin/msfadmin falls instantly.
steps.code:
hydra -l msfadmin -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -t 4 -V -f 192.168.1.10 ssh
# [22][ssh] host: 192.168.1.10 login: msfadmin password: msfadmin
steps.desc: Brute-force SSH on your own Metasploitable VM:
steps.title: Step 1 — SSH Brute Force

steps.box: FTP logins often share the same weak credentials as SSH on lab VMs. Same flags, different module — Hydra's service list covers 50+ protocols.
steps.code:
hydra -L users.txt -P passwords.txt -t 4 192.168.1.10 ftp
# [21][ftp] login: msfadmin password: msfadmin
steps.desc: Try FTP with user and password lists:
steps.title: Step 2 — FTP Brute Force

steps.box: The failure string is everything: Hydra decides success vs failure by its presence. Copy it exactly from a real failed login or every attempt reads as success.
steps.code:
hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt localhost http-post-form "/dvwa/login.php:username=^USER^&password=^PASS^:Login failed"
# [80][http-post-form] login: admin password: password
steps.desc: Attack a DVWA login form (your localhost only):
steps.title: Step 3 — Web Form Brute Force

steps.box: Account lockouts and fail2ban exist because of exactly this traffic. Tune -t down, add -w seconds between tries, and stop when the lab policy would lock you.
steps.code:
hydra -l admin -P small.txt -t 1 -w 2 192.168.1.10 ssh
# 1 task, 2s wait: slow but stealthy
steps.desc: Slow the attack to dodge lockouts in shared labs:
steps.title: Step 4 — Slow & Quiet Mode
